note: A twelve-year police officer, now a detective in a technology unit — a stable public-service career, not a business owner, physician or equivalent, so 'successful' fails as the criterion is written even though he is plainly established and promoted. Income holds on his own account: he never claimed he could not pay and said 'I would think that I would have the money to do it, even if I have to put it on a credit card', with the friction being cash timing ahead of a Christmas due date rather than capacity. Health is squarely the neglected area now — he is doing nothing, has a garage gym he cannot use and self-rates his energy at half what it was — and the acute crisis is roughly two years behind him. He is not remotely the excluded profile: 140 lb, a near-professional baseball player through college, and someone who built a gym at home. Good-to-great is the clean miss. At 140 lb with a plateau he cannot break, an unresolved shoulder and no current training, he is buying his way back to a former baseline of 155-160, which is rescue rather than refinement, and he says so — 'just wanting to get back to where I was.' Worth recording against the corpus for a different reason: the ICP screens for people whose problem is neglect, and this prospect's problem is illness. Nothing in the stated criteria distinguishes a man who let his health slide from a man whose health collapsed and is still relapsing, and those two need very different handling.
